2. Heard learned counsel for petitioners and Sri Farhan- Azam Khan, learned Standing Counsel for Waqf Board.

3. This Court on 30.11.2016 in Writ Petition No.7324 of 2003 passed the following order;
"Petitioners earlier filed Writ Petition No.26273 of 2023 to declare the action of the Joint Collector in passing the Award in favour of the Waqf Board in respect of the land in an extent of Acs.2.30 guntas situated in Survey No.2149 of Vemsoor Village and Mandal, Khammam District, without considering the claim of petitioners.

In the said Writ Petiton, this Court passed the order dated 21.09.2023 to the following effect:
"The dispute in this Writ Petition is with regard to the claim of compensation in respect of land admeasuring Ac.2-30 Ya gantas, situated in survey No.2149 of Vemsoor Village and Mandal, Khammam District, which is acquired by respondent No.3 for the IA No.2 of 2023 purpose of four laning of National High Way by passing an Award No.Gl/219112019-3, dated 11.01.2022.
In the said Award, compensation was awarded in favour of respondent No.6, whereas the petitioners herein are making rival claim for payment of compensation in respect of the said extent of land.

From the material on record, it appears that already there is existing dispute between the petitioners and respondent No.6, which is pending before this Court in W.P.No.7976 of 2020, wherein this Court directed the respondents therein including the Waqf Board not to interfere with the possession and enjoyment of the petitioners therein on various extents including the land in Survey No.2149 admeasuring Acs.24-01 guntas.
The said writ petition is still pending for consideration.

In the circumstances, prima facie, award of compensation amount in favour of respondent Mohammad Jamaluddin vs Sri Syed Khajamoinuddin on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57228005/

sentences.text: In case, there are rival claims for payment of compensation, the Acquisition Authority cannot decide the same, but it is appropriate to refer the matter under Section 76 to the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority for adjudication of the rival claims.

In the circumstances, pending further orders, there shall be interim direction directing the respondents not to disburse the compensation pursuant to the Award, dated 11.01.2022, in respect of the subject land."

Now, in this case, the grievance of petitioners is that despite the said order, the 3rd respondent-Joint Collector sent the compensation amount to the account of the Waqf Board on 29.09.2023 through RTGS, as is evident from their affidavit in vacate stay petition filed in Writ Petition No.26598 of 2023.
It appears, the said order was not understood by the respondents in its letter and spirit.
Hence, there shall be a direction to the 1st respondent to remit compensation amount pursuant to the Award dated 11.01.2022 to the 3rd respondent in a week from today.
Post the Writ Petition before the Court hearing the subject issues."

4. Today, learned Standing Counsel, by placing on record letter dated 05.12.2024 of the 2nd respondent submits that the order dated 19.04.2024 has been complied with as a Demand Draft bearing No.375536, dated 04.12.2024 for Rs.64,66,615/- drawn in favour of the Additional Collector/Joint Collector-cum-competent Authority for Land Acquisition has been issued.
5. The submission made by the learned Standing Counsel is not disputed by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
6. In view of the letter dated 05.12.2024 placed by learned Standing Counsel with regard to compliance of the orders dated 19.04.2024 in W.P.No.6984 of 2024, this Contempt Case is closed.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
